name: Teenage Fanclub
label: Creation
lede: Three songwriters from Glasgow sold a neighbour's fridge to make a debut, then a moneybag sleeve beat Nirvana in Spin and drew a letter from Gene Simmons.

eras.title: Paid for by a neighbour's appliances
eras.text: Out of the ashes of The Boy Hairdressers, Norman Blake, Raymond McGinley and Gerard Love made a noisy, sludgy first album on almost no money. Matador Records put it out in America, and the tiny New York label suddenly had people paying attention.

years.h: The Boy Hairdressers split, and Teenage Fanclub starts up in Glasgow
years.p: Norman Blake, Raymond McGinley and drummer Francis MacDonald start a new band, and bassist Gerard Love joins soon after. All three frontline members write and sing.

years.big: "Raymond sold a fridge and a washing machine his neighbour had left him"
years.h: A neighbour's fridge pays for the first album
years.p: Teenage Fanclub records A Catholic Education from July to December 1989 at Pet Sounds in Glasgow and Suite 16 in Rochdale. McGinley sold the appliances to cover it.
years.xp: The quote is Norman Blake's. By his account the neighbour left the fridge and washing machine behind, McGinley sold them, and the money paid for the sessions.

years.h: Francis MacDonald goes back to university; Brendan O'Hare takes the drums
years.p: MacDonald lays down his drum parts and returns to his studies. [[Brendan O'Hare|9f1ead0a-9176-48fd-8c05-ecdbf28ca5ce]] replaces him, and the band re-records four songs so he is on the album.

years.src: Wikipedia: A Catholic Education · Wikipedia: Matador Records
years.h: A Catholic Education sounds like grunge, bar one song
years.p: The debut comes out on Paperhouse in the UK on June 11, led by the single Everything Flows. Matador Records issues it in North America on August 2.
years.xp:
AllMusic's Jason Ankeny later called its sound gloriously sloppy and sludgy, closer to grunge than to the power pop the band became known for. Everything Flows is the exception, the one song that sounds like the band to come.

For Matador it was the first real attention the young label got.

eras.title: Album of the year, over Nirvana
eras.text: Signed to Creation Records in Britain and Geffen in America, the band went to Liverpool with Don Fleming and came back singing in harmony. Spin put the result above Nevermind, and Kurt Cobain kept bringing them up.

years.h: Teenage Fanclub makes The King overnight, and Creation deletes it
years.p: Recorded in one day at Amazon Studios during the Bandwagonesque sessions, with covers of Madonna's Like a Virgin and Pink Floyd's Interstellar Overdrive.
years.xp:
Norman Blake said the band got completely wasted one night and decided to make an LP overnight. Matador's Gerard Cosloy said in 2020 that the label had rejected it as a second album, seeing it as a contract-filler; the band blamed the chaos on Don Fleming's love of improvising.

Creation meant it as a 500–1,000 copy budget release but pressed 10,000–20,000 at full price, then pulled it. It still reached No. 53 in the UK and became a collector's item.

yt: What You Do To Me, official video
years.h: Don Fleming takes the band to Liverpool for Bandwagonesque
years.p: Recorded at Amazon Studios from April 9 to May 12, 1991. [[Don Fleming|deae7f43-894e-45f1-ae34-08bc0c921b82]] pushed the vocal harmonies, and every member wrote. Star Sign reaches No. 4 on Billboard's Modern Rock chart.
years.xp: The album peaked at No. 22 in the UK and No. 137 in the US. Sharon Fitzgerald designed the cover and took the photograph on it.

years.h: Gene Simmons sends Geffen a letter about the moneybag
years.p: Sharon Fitzgerald's Bandwagonesque cover shows a moneybag with a dollar sign. [[Kiss|e1f1e33e-2e4c-4d43-b91b-7064068d3283]]'s [[Gene Simmons|96a1182f-e8e6-4df6-a811-82cb67d4565c]], who had trademarked a moneybag logo, complained to Geffen.
years.xp: According to Simmons's book Sex Money Kiss, Geffen gave in and sent him a cheque. No amount is given.

yt: What You Do To Me on The Word, January 1992
years.h: Spin ranks Bandwagonesque above Nevermind
years.p: Spin's 1991 album of the year goes to Teenage Fanclub, ahead of [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s Nevermind and [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]]'s Out of Time.
years.xp: The magazine has since both apologized for the pick and defended it.

years.h: Kurt Cobain keeps saying it, then Nirvana takes them on tour
years.p: [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] name-checked Teenage Fanclub in interview after interview. In summer 1992 they support [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] on the road.

eras.title: Top ten at home
eras.text: After a fussed-over third album and a drummer change, the band cleaned up its sound and became a top-ten act in Britain. Their Creation labelmates in Oasis ranked them second, behind themselves.

years.src: Wikipedia: Thirteen (Teenage Fanclub album) · Wikipedia: Teenage Fanclub
years.h: Thirteen gets bad reviews, then a second look
years.p: Recorded over months in Glasgow and near Manchester and self-produced. Norman Blake says the title counts the songs, not the [[Big Star|21d177ba-3d51-461e-9b3f-ad9a80b419dc]] tune.
years.xp:
Blake said the band went in with 40 fragments of songs and kept revising and re-recording. Geffen's art department pitched a sleeve of a crying girl with running mascara; Blake felt they were trying to sell the band to teenage girls. The band paid £10,000 in fees and made its own cover, inspired by Jeff Koons' basketballs.

The lead single Radio reached No. 31 in the UK.

years.h: Brendan O'Hare leaves, and Paul Quinn of the Soup Dragons takes over
years.p: After the Thirteen tour the band parts with its drummer over musical differences. [[Paul Quinn|ec558ca2-811c-47b8-b671-b23a826d6f5e]], formerly of [[The Soup Dragons|5c42c9cf-5833-41d8-b600-177e70894046]], takes the kit. O'Hare later spends about a year in [[Mogwai|d700b3f5-45af-4d02-95ed-57d301bda93e]].

years.h: Grand Prix puts a Formula One car on the cover and the band in the top ten
years.p: Recorded at the Manor in Oxfordshire with David Bianco, it reaches No. 7. The car is a racer lent by the Simtek team. Singles: Mellow Doubt, Sparky's Dream, Neil Jung.
years.xp: Sessions ran from September 5 to October 9, 1994, with Bianco and the band producing. The Guardian's Adam Sweeting made it CD of the week and NME gave it 9/10; in 2018 Q placed it at No. 72 on its list of the 100 greatest British albums. It went Silver in the UK.

years.h: Liam Gallagher ranks them second, right behind Oasis
years.p: [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]]'s singer, a Creation labelmate, puts Teenage Fanclub just under his own band.

years.h: Songs from Northern Britain reaches No. 3 in the UK
years.p: Teenage Fanclub's biggest UK album. Ain't That Enough reaches No. 17, their highest-charting single. The band tours with [[Radiohead|a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711]], but the album doesn't chart in America.
years.xp: Sessions ran from Surrey's Ridge Farm to London's AIR Studios. Midway through, the band fell out with producer David Bianco, and George Shilling finished the job. Nick Hornby later championed the record in his book 31 Songs.

years.h: Finlay MacDonald joins on keyboards
years.p: Finlay MacDonald plays keyboards, guitar and bass with the band until 2001.

eras.title: Creation folds, the band starts its own label
eras.text: Creation collapsed, Sony came and went, and the band ended up releasing records on its own PeMa label. The original drummer came back, the records slowed down, and nobody hurried.

years.h: With Creation gone, Howdy! goes to Columbia
years.p: Paul Quinn leaves after recording his parts, citing personal difficulties within the band. Original drummer Francis MacDonald comes back.

years.h: A whole album with Jad Fair of Half Japanese
years.p: Words of Wisdom and Hope teams Teenage Fanclub with [[Jad Fair|be4a8e65-a7ba-474c-989b-ed16e51c1a39]] of [[Half Japanese|18dc6bd7-9caa-4c2d-a2fc-e9546ebda6a4]]. A Sony best-of with one new song from each writer follows.

years.h: John McEntire of Tortoise produces Man-Made in Chicago
years.p: Recorded in 2004 with [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]] of [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]] and released on the band's own PeMa label.

years.cap: Teenage Fanclub at the Barrowlands, Glasgow, September 29, 2006
years.h: Bandwagonesque start to finish, London and Glasgow
years.p: Two special concerts play the whole 1991 album in order.

years.cap: Teenage Fanclub at Summer Sundae, Leicester, August 2010
years.h: Three weeks at a Norfolk farm make Shadows
years.p: Recorded at Leeders Farm from August 2008, with Dave McGowan now a full member. PeMa releases it in Europe; Merge Records issues it in North America on June 8.

years.cap: Teenage Fanclub on stage at Sonorama, August 2011
years.h: Teenage Fanclub backs Edwyn Collins at Belle and Sebastian's Bowlie 2
years.p: At the ATP festival [[Belle and Sebastian|e5c7b94f-e264-473c-bb0f-37c85d4d5c70]] curate, the band serves as [[Edwyn Collins|14c0c282-e0c1-46fe-acd1-9a015ba721c5]]'s band, including [[Orange Juice|e598d30e-4ce1-402e-94a7-6f44779da6b7]]'s Rip It Up.

eras.title: Gerard Love's last lap
eras.text: The band took support slots at stadiums, made its tenth album and remastered its Creation records at Abbey Road. The victory lap brought back two old drummers and followed a founder's exit.

years.h: Old Trafford, opening for Foo Fighters
years.p: Teenage Fanclub supports [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]] at the cricket ground in Manchester.

years.h: Here is the last album with Gerard Love
years.p: Teenage Fanclub's tenth studio record.

years.h: Ben Gibbard covers all of Bandwagonesque
years.p: [[Death Cab for Cutie|0039c7ae-e1a7-4a7d-9b49-0cbc716821a6]]'s [[Ben Gibbard|02031e5c-f9ab-4b4e-bc08-a61ea11a455d]] records the whole album, calling it his favorite record by his favorite band. The documentary Teenage Superstars tells the band's early story the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Teenage Fanclub · Wikipedia: Gerard Love
years.h: Gerard Love quits rather than fly
years.p: Love announces that the upcoming Creation Years shows will be his last. He didn't want to fly frequently for international dates, and the band says the split was over future touring.
years.xp: Love wrote many of the band's best-known songs and shared lead vocals from the start. He later records as [[Lightships|b7a02d12-2db2-4489-8e04-24af4f597795]], whose 2012 album Electric Cables featured Dave McGowan and Brendan O'Hare.

years.h: Both old drummers return for the Creation Years tour
years.p: After remastering five Creation albums at Abbey Road, the band plays three nights each in Glasgow, Manchester, Birmingham and London. Brendan O'Hare and Paul Quinn drum on the albums they made.
years.xp: The four-city run took place in October and November 2018.

eras.title: The Euros Childs line-up
eras.text: A reshuffled band with Gorky's Zygotic Mynci's Euros Childs on keys made two albums, one of them trapped behind a pandemic.

years.h: Euros Childs takes the keyboards; Dave McGowan moves to bass
years.p: Euros Childs, Norman Blake's partner in the duo Jonny, joins after Love's exit. McGowan, also in [[Belle and Sebastian|e5c7b94f-e264-473c-bb0f-37c85d4d5c70]] since 2018, switches to bass.

years.h: Endless Arcade waits out COVID-19
years.p: Recorded in 2019 and due in October 2020, the album slips repeatedly, along with four rounds of rescheduled tour dates.

years.h: Twelve albums in, Nothing Lasts Forever
years.p: Announced on May 23, 2023, the twelfth album arrives that September.
